summary: Corrected PLAN.md status against measured facts (58 tests in 5 files, 77 catalogued, 150 of 160 specs still placeholders, 77/77 REA), added the Unreleased 0.3.3 release notes to CHANGELOG.md, and added docs/release-process.md with the SemVer mapping, the full verification checklist and the maintainer approval gate; registered the page in the docs index and site page list and regenerated the site.

commands.command: for f in products/*/*/package.json; do (cd "$(dirname "$f")" && npm test) || exit 1; done

checksNotRun: npm publish, git tag and push: blocked on maintainer approval, as AGENTS.md and the new release-process.md require.
GitHub Pages deploy: not triggered; it runs from CI on main after a push.
Vercel deploy: not attempted; the canonical origin is now GitHub Pages and Vercel is opt-in via REA_SITE_URL.
decisions: Proposed 0.3.3 as a patch: no CLI command, flag, schema or catalog record changed; the substantive fixes are test scripts, the canonical origin and documentation. The bump itself is deliberately left to the release step so it can land with the changelog section.
PLAN.md now states measured numbers instead of the stale 56 tests and all-placeholder specs; the 15 remaining workspaces are named as pending rather than implied done.
Release notes live under CHANGELOG [Unreleased] instead of a separate notes file, so there is one release record; docs/release-process.md describes how to promote that section.
risks: The site rebuild touches 89 generated pages because every page carries the docs navigation; the substantive changes are the added release-process page and the sitemap/robots origin.
docs/research-batches.md and PLAN.md hold 2026-11-02 snapshots; the count guard covers README, skills index and site metrics, but not prose status tables.
Nothing was published, tagged or committed; the release remains worktree-only.
recommendedNextAction: Have the maintainer review the 0.3.3 changelog section and release checklist, then bump the version with npm version patch --no-git-tag-version and publish from an approved release.
